title: Decluttr Alternatives for Phones, Tech, CDs and Books
summary: Here are the best Decluttr alternatives for selling phones, tech, books, CDs, DVDs and games.
body_markdown:
Decluttr has officially closed, so if you used it to sell your old phone, CDs, DVDs, games or books, you’ll need a new place to sell them. The best Decluttr alternatives depend on what you have: Gazelle, ecoATM and Back Market for phones and tech, BookScouter for books, and eBay or Mercari for CDs, DVDs and games.


## Main Takeaways


- Decluttr has closed, so you’ll need a new place to sell your phones, tech, CDs, DVDs, games and books.
- For phones and tech, buyback sites like Gazelle and ecoATM are the easiest options.
- For books, BookScouter shows you the best buyback offer for each one.
- For CDs, DVDs and games, selling them yourself on eBay or Mercari is your best bet.
- Vendoo lets you list each item once and sell it on several marketplaces.


## What Happened to Decluttr?


[Decluttr](https://www.decluttr.com/) has closed and isn’t buying anything anymore. Its parent company, musicMagpie,[shut down its US business](https://ng.investing.com/news/company-news/ao-ltd-to-shut-down-musicmagpies-us-operations-93CH-1946378) , and currently, Decluttr’s customer service is only handling orders that were already in progress.


## The Best Decluttr Alternatives in 2026


The best Decluttr alternative depends on what you’re selling. Let’s take a look at the most common categories:

## Phones and Tech


### **Gazelle**


[Gazelle](https://www.gazelle.com/iphone) buys phones, iPads and MacBooks by mail. You get an instant offer online, and if you accept, Gazelle emails you a prepaid shipping label. Once they inspect your device, you’re paid by check, PayPal or Amazon gift card.


### **ecoATM**


[ecoATM](https://www.ecoatm.com/pages/how-it-works-1) is the fastest option if you want money ASAP. Lock in an offer online for 7 days, then drop your phone at a kiosk and get paid on the spot with cash, Venmo or PayPal. You’ll need to bring a valid photo ID, because the kiosk scans it before you can sell, and you have to be 18 or older.


### **Back Market Trade-In**


[Back Market](https://www.backmarket.com/en-us/buyback/home) matches your device with the highest offer from the more than 250 refurbishers it works with. Your offer is good for 21 days, shipping is free and you’re paid by direct deposit.


### **Swappa**


[Swappa](https://swappa.com/blog/how-swappa-works/) is a marketplace where you sell your items directly to another person instead of a company. Listing is free, and Swappa says sellers pay no fees because the buyer covers them. You’re paid through PayPal as soon as your item sells.


### **BuyBackWorld**


[BuyBackWorld](https://www.buybackworld.com/) buys phones, iPads, MacBooks and game consoles. Quotes are guaranteed for 30 days and shipping is free.


### **Apple Trade In and Best Buy Trade-In**


Both are easy if you’re already shopping there since they don’t give cash.[Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/trade-in) gives you credit toward a purchase or an Apple Gift Card, and[Best Buy](https://www.bestbuy.com/trade-in) pays with a Best Buy gift card.


### **SellCell**


[SellCell](https://www.sellcell.com/brands/decluttr/) doesn’t buy anything itself. It compares the prices of over 40 buyers so you can pick the best offer.


## Books


### **BookScouter**


[BookScouter](https://bookscouter.com/) is the closest thing to selling books on Decluttr. Enter or scan the ISBN, and it shows offers from 30+ vendors so you can pick the highest one. It doesn’t buy books itself, so you sell to whichever vendor you choose.


## CDs, DVDs and Games


### **eBay and Mercari**


There’s no direct buyback replacement for Decluttr when it comes to CDs, DVDs and games, so your best option is to sell them yourself on eBay or Mercari.


## Instant Buyback vs. Selling It Yourself


Buyback sites are faster and easier, but selling it yourself almost always gets you more money. With a buyback site, you get an offer in minutes, ship the item for free and get paid without dealing with buyers yourself. That convenience costs you, though. When you sell it yourself, you set the price and keep more of the sale, but you take the photos, write the listing and ship it.


#### **Fees When You Sell It Yourself**


Selling yourself isn’t free. Here’s what two of the most popular marketplaces charge:


- **[eBay](https://www.ebay.com/help/selling/fees-credits-invoices/selling-fees?id=4822) :** about 13.6% on the total amount of the sale up to $7,500 for most categories, and 15.3% for books, movies and music. eBay also charges a per-order fee: for orders $10.00 or less the per order fee is $0.30, for orders over $10.00 the per order fee is $0.40.
- **[Mercari](https://www.mercari.com/us/help_center/article/169/) :** a flat 10% selling fee.


To see exactly what you’d keep, run your numbers through our[marketplace fee calculator](https://www.vendoo.co/marketplaces-fee-calculator) .


## Sell Your Tech, CDs and Books Everywhere With Vendoo


If you want more than a buyback offer, Vendoo is the easiest way to replace Decluttr: you sell your items yourself on several marketplaces at once. This gets more buyers looking at each item without spending time manually crosslisting.


### **Crosslist Everything**


Create one listing in Vendoo and send it to top marketplaces including eBay, Poshmark, Mercari, Depop, Facebook Marketplace, Grailed, Vinted, Vestiaire Collective, Shopify, Whatnot, and Etsy. So your phone, a game or a boxed set can be in front of buyers on several sites at once.


### **Save Time on Media**


Listing templates make a big difference when you’re listing lots of similar items like CDs, DVDs or games. You can create templates for different categories or for items that share the same details, so you only fill in what changes.


### **No Double Sales**


When an item sells, Vendoo’s Sale Detection and Auto Delist catches it and removes it from your other marketplaces, so you don’t sell the same DVD twice.


### **Pricing**


Vendoo starts at $14.99 a month, or $12.49 a month billed yearly, and you can try it free for 14 days.


## Conclusion


With Decluttr closed, there’s no single site that buys everything it used to. For phones and tech, a buyback site like Gazelle, ecoATM or Back Market is the quickest swap. For books, start with BookScouter. For CDs, DVDs and games, selling them yourself on eBay or Mercari is your best bet, and crosslisting with Vendoo gets each item in front of more buyers so it sells faster.


## FAQs


### **What happened to Decluttr?**


Decluttr has closed and is no longer buying phones, tech, CDs, DVDs, games or books. Its parent company, musicMagpie, shut down its US business. Decluttr’s customer service is still handling orders that were already in progress, so contact them if you’re waiting on payment for an item you sent in.


### **Is Decluttr coming back?**


The website says it has closed, and customer service is only handling orders that were already in progress. For now, sellers need to use other options.


### **What is the best site like Decluttr?**


It depends on what you’re selling. For phones and tech, Gazelle, ecoATM and Back Market Trade-In work a lot like Decluttr did. For books, BookScouter compares offers from 30+ buyers. For CDs, DVDs and games, there’s no real buyback replacement, so selling on eBay or Mercari is your best option.


### **Where can I sell CDs and DVDs now that Decluttr is closed?**


Your best option is to sell them yourself on eBay or Mercari. Listing on both with a crosslisting tool like Vendoo gets each item in front of more buyers.


### **Is it better to use a buyback site or sell it yourself?**


Buyback sites are faster and easier: you get an instant offer, ship for free and get paid without dealing with buyers. Selling it yourself on eBay or Mercari usually gets you more money, but you handle the photos, listing, questions and shipping. For valuable tech, selling yourself is often worth it.
